g.text: N1 [Context]
reasoning LLMs scale test-time compute
Reasoning LLMs enable test-time scaling: Spending more reasoning tokens
often yields better performance (DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025; Snell et al.,
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=2) Reasoning LLMs enable test-time scaling: Spending more reasoning tokens often yields better performance (DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025; Snell et al., 2024).

g.text: N2 [Context]
challenge: adaptive instance-aware stopping
However, a practical challenge of reasoning LLMs lies in inducing adaptive
reasoning behavior that adjusts to instance difficulty—deciding when
additional thinking is still useful versus wasteful.
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=0) However, a practical challenge of reasoning LLMs lies in inducing adaptive reasoning behavior that adjusts to instance difficulty—deciding when additional thinking is still useful versus wasteful.

g.text: N3 [Prior_Work]
adaptive thinking via uncertainty thresholds
Recent works propose adaptive thinking mechanisms (Wang et al., 2025a; Yang
et al., 2025; Fu et al., 2025) by monitoring the reasoning model's
uncertainty in the answer (e.g. by measuring confidence or entropy), and
when uncertainty falls…
g.title: N3 [Prior_Work] (cites=3) Recent works propose adaptive thinking mechanisms (Wang et al., 2025a; Yang et al., 2025; Fu et al., 2025) by monitoring the reasoning model's uncertainty in the answer (e.g. by measuring confidence or entropy), and when uncertainty falls below a pre-defined threshold, the reasoning is halted.

g.text: N4 [Prior_Work]
instance-dependent token budgets
Adaptive thinking enables instance-dependent token budgets, since the
reasoning effort required to reach a confident threshold varies by problem.
g.title: N4 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) Adaptive thinking enables instance-dependent token budgets, since the reasoning effort required to reach a confident threshold varies by problem.

g.text: N5 [Limitation]
adaptive thinking just shifts the knob
However, adaptive thinking does not alleviate the practical challenge of
setting reasoning budget; it only converts the problem of setting a token
budget into setting a threshold.
g.title: N5 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, adaptive thinking does not alleviate the practical challenge of setting reasoning budget; it only converts the problem of setting a token budget into setting a threshold.

g.text: N6 [Limitation]
thresholds lack interpretable meaning
In fact, setting a threshold could be trickier than setting a token budget
since the threshold value often lacks interpretable meaning, and could lie
in arbitrary ranges depending on how the uncertainty is computed (Figure. 1,
left).
g.title: N6 [Limitation] (cites=0) In fact, setting a threshold could be trickier than setting a token budget since the threshold value often lacks interpretable meaning, and could lie in arbitrary ranges depending on how the uncertainty is computed (Figure. 1, left).

g.text: N7 [Method]
principled stopping-rule framework
In this paper, we provide a principled framework for setting stopping rules
for adaptive reasoning.
g.title: N7 [Method] (cites=0) In this paper, we provide a principled framework for setting stopping rules for adaptive reasoning.

g.text: N8 [Method]
early termination = risk of error
In particular, we leverage a key implication of test-time scaling: any early
termination of reasoning introduces a risk of error.
g.title: N8 [Method] (cites=0) In particular, we leverage a key implication of test-time scaling: any early termination of reasoning introduces a risk of error.

g.text: N9 [Method]
reframe budget as choosing risk
Based on this observation, we reframe the problem of setting a reasoning
budget as choosing an acceptable level of risk, an interpretable quantity
that directly interfaces with downstream decision-making pipelines.
g.title: N9 [Method] (cites=0) Based on this observation, we reframe the problem of setting a reasoning budget as choosing an acceptable level of risk, an interpretable quantity that directly interfaces with downstream decision-making pipelines.

g.text: N10 [Method]
distribution-free risk control mapping
We utilize an external validation set and distribution-free risk control
framework (Bates et al., 2021; Jazbec et al., 2024) to automatically map a
user-specified risk to the corresponding criteria for terminating the
reasoning chain.
g.title: N10 [Method] (cites=2) We utilize an external validation set and distribution-free risk control framework (Bates et al., 2021; Jazbec et al., 2024) to automatically map a user-specified risk to the corresponding criteria for terminating the reasoning chain.

g.text: N11 [Method: dual-threshold]
two risks: upper + novel lower threshold
Specifically, we delineate two complementary types of risks and their
corresponding controlling mechanisms (illustrated in Fig. 2): False positive
risk of thinking the model has the correct answer, controlled by an upper
threshold of…
g.title: N11 [Method: dual-threshold] (cites=0) Specifically, we delineate two complementary types of risks and their corresponding controlling mechanisms (illustrated in Fig. 2): False positive risk of thinking the model has the correct answer, controlled by an upper threshold of confidence; False negative risk of thinking the current (and future) answers will be incorrect, controlled by the lower threshold, a novel mechanism that measures whether the reasoning is making enough progress.

g.text: N12 [Method: dual-threshold]
two thresholds target two inefficiencies
These two types of risks and thresholds are related to different sources of
inefficiency: The upper threshold reduces wasted tokens after the model has
effectively converged (Eq. (8)), while the lower threshold avoids spending
tokens when…
g.title: N12 [Method: dual-threshold] (cites=0) These two types of risks and thresholds are related to different sources of inefficiency: The upper threshold reduces wasted tokens after the model has effectively converged (Eq. (8)), while the lower threshold avoids spending tokens when further reasoning is unlikely to help (Eq. (9)).

g.text: N13a [Contribution: Contribution 1]
loss functions + risk control
(i) We introduce a collection of loss functions that capture
different sources of inefficiency and errors from early stopping,
enabling incorporation of distribution-free risk control into
reasoning LLMs, a principled approach that allows…
g.title: N13a [Contribution: Contribution 1] (cites=0) (i) We introduce a collection of loss functions that capture different sources of inefficiency and errors from early stopping, enabling incorporation of distribution-free risk control into reasoning LLMs, a principled approach that allows early stopping (Sec. 4.1);

g.text: N13b [Contribution: Contribution 2]
novel parametric lower threshold
(ii) We introduce a novel parametric lower threshold that halts
the reasoning when the model is not progressing sufficiently at
decreasing uncertainty (Sec. 4.2);
g.title: N13b [Contribution: Contribution 2] (cites=0) (ii) We introduce a novel parametric lower threshold that halts the reasoning when the model is not progressing sufficiently at decreasing uncertainty (Sec. 4.2);

g.text: N13c [Contribution: Contribution 3]
upper+lower yields efficiency gains
(iii) We demonstrate that at the same risk level, different
approaches exhibit different efficiency, whereas using our upper
threshold plus our proposed parametric lower threshold
consistently yields efficiency gains (Sec. 5.3).
g.title: N13c [Contribution: Contribution 3] (cites=0) (iii) We demonstrate that at the same risk level, different approaches exhibit different efficiency, whereas using our upper threshold plus our proposed parametric lower threshold consistently yields efficiency gains (Sec. 5.3).

g.text: P1 [Proof]
Fig. 1: signal/method-dependent thresholds
Figure 1. Early-stopping behavior under different target test
risks. Left: Threshold values required to achieve a given target
test risk vary substantially across early-stopping signals,
indicating that threshold selection is…
g.title: P1 [Proof] (cites=0) Figure 1. Early-stopping behavior under different target test risks. Left: Threshold values required to achieve a given target test risk vary substantially across early-stopping signals, indicating that threshold selection is signal-dependent. Right: The relative efficiency of different early-stopping methods depends on the target test risk, and no single method is uniformly most efficient across all risk levels.

g.text: P2 [Proof]
Fig. 2: dual-threshold trajectories on AIME
Figure 2. Dual-threshold early exit via risk-controlled confidence
dynamics. We plot confidence trajectories as a function of token
usage under Qwen3-8B on AIME questions. Left: an unsolvable
instance, model confidence fluctuates and fails…
g.title: P2 [Proof] (cites=0) Figure 2. Dual-threshold early exit via risk-controlled confidence dynamics. We plot confidence trajectories as a function of token usage under Qwen3-8B on AIME questions. Left: an unsolvable instance, model confidence fluctuates and fails to reach the upper threshold; the reasoning is halted early by the parametric lower threshold, preventing unnecessary token consumption. Right: a solvable instance, where confidence steadily increases and crosses the upper threshold, triggering termination once sufficient confidence is achieved.
